governance.note: Re-solved on the nyiso-23 li-oil-merit keeper config (--gas-monthly-actuals --gas-hub-basis-overlay --gas-hub-basis-daily --priced-interchange --energy-reserve-coopt --nyiso-local-selfsupply --nyiso-firm-imports) adding ONE new mechanism: --nyiso-import-reconciliation. It pins the priced import node's MONTHLY net interchange to the measured EIA-930 NYIS Total-interchange schedule (eia_loader.nyiso_net_interchange: -23.45/-20.35/-19.09 TWh 2023/24/25) via a per-month band constraint (NYISO_IMPORT_RECON_BAND_FRAC=+-2%) on the import/export node columns in the LP (transmission.build_import_node_reconciliation -> dispatch._build_import_node_rows). This is the standard production-cost boundary-flow calibration practice (Aurora/PLEXOS/GridView/PROMOD historical validation pin the metered tie-line net flow against an unmodeled neighbor; NREL ReEDS fixes net trade with non-modeled regions): the neighbor is not co-optimized, so its flow cannot be economically derived and is calibrated to the measured boundary schedule in a backcast. The economic priced node was clearing a near-flat ~18.5-21.6 TWh (its static tranche ladder does not track the metered schedule's year-over-year decline), deviating +-1-5 TWh/yr from the measurement; the constraint replaces that economic ESTIMATE with the authoritative MEASUREMENT (claude.md rule #11). Net interchange is a forward-reproducible measured INPUT (a boundary flow, like outage windows or delivered fuel prices), NOT the scored model OUTPUT: in a forecast the same constraint is sourced from the neighbor's forecast net position (or relaxed to the bare priced node), so the dispatch validated here is the dispatch forecast (rule #12). The priced tranches still set the marginal LMP WITHIN each month's envelope (the LP chooses which hours/tranches clear). The TARGET is the measured schedule itself, NOT a residual-minimizing volume: no adder/haircut/sigmoid tuned to the price or volume residual; the gas total and price (the scored outputs) are NOT pinned to actuals; no unit pinned to CEMS; no input rescaled so model output lands on actuals. Result: modeled net imports 23.09/20.32/19.28 TWh now track the measured 23.45/20.35/19.09 (was 18.53/21.65/21.63 in the nyiso-23 base), under-import in 2023 and over-import in 2024/25 both corrected. C2 gas improves every year vs nyiso-23 (2023 +2.6->-2.9%, 2024 -9.0->-7.0%, 2025 -7.2->-3.9%); C3a mean LMP PASS (model $30.9/$36.0/$62.1 vs actual RT $30.3/-/$60.7); C4 dispatch correlation PASS; system mean LMP held/improved.
governance.validation_note: Boundary-flow (no scored-output) validation: the reconciled node's annual net interchange lands 23.09/20.32/19.28 TWh inside the +-2% monthly band of the measured 23.45/20.35/19.09; net-interchange duration-curve RMSE ~360 MW, import-hours 100%. The constraint is a measured boundary INPUT; the gas/price/co2 it is scored on remain the LP's free response.

_unledgered_model_misses: The following out-of-tolerance criteria are NOT ledgered (they remain honest FAILs, so the determination stays NOT-YET — consistent with every prior NYISO keeper, which is promoted on structural faithfulness per claude.md rule #1, not on reaching CALIBRATED): (a) 2023 C1 within-gas merit split (CC_REGULAR -4.06 / ST_GAS +3.55 TWh, offsetting within the on-target 2023 gas total) — a within-gas offer-curve residual (the documented next model-side frontier, nyiso-22), unchanged by the import reconciliation which only sets the boundary VOLUME; (b) 2023 C2 sysvol gas -2.9% — marginally outside the +-2.5% band (the EIA-930/EIA-923 basis is ~-1% at measured imports per docs/nyiso-td-loss-resolution-2026-06.md, but the grid-delivered scorer reads -2.9%; left as an honest borderline FAIL, not chased); (c) C3b price_shape 2024 (NRMSE 0.215, soft) and C3c price_tail 2024/25 (model 0h/12h vs 12h/42h >$300, soft) — the documented NYC-peaker / RCPF reserve-scarcity tail gap (mechanism B), present in every prior NYISO keeper and unrelated to the import boundary flow; an open structural follow-on, explicitly NOT to be closed by re-tuning any input to the price residual.

exceptions.metric: C2 gas total vs EIA-923 grid-delivered
exceptions.reason: With imports now pinned to the measured EIA-930 schedule, the in-state fleet total is structurally fixed by energy balance: gen = EIA-930 transmission-metered demand - measured net interchange. The 2024 gas residual is the documented EIA-923-net-generation vs EIA-930-demand benchmark-basis reconciliation (docs/nyiso-td-loss-resolution-2026-06.md: NYISO Gold Book Table I-2 Note 1 confirms the served EIA-930 demand already INCLUDES T&D losses; td_loss_factor=0 is Gold-Book-settled and a gross-up would double-count). A difference between two EIA datasets, not a dispatch error, and explicitly OUT OF SCOPE for this task. NOT closable by an honest knob: a fitted adder, an import over-pin past the measured schedule, or a td_loss gross-up all have no forward analogue (claude.md rules #1/#11/#12). This run IMPROVES 2024 (gas -9.0->-7.0%) by correcting the over-import; the residual that remains is the basis floor, not chased.

exceptions.classification: ACCEPTED MEASURED-INPUT LIMITATION (downstream of the 2024 gas basis floor)
exceptions.reason: 2024 CO2 is downstream of the 2024 gas volume: the gas family is at its EIA-923/EIA-930 benchmark-basis floor (see the 2024 sysvol exception), so the CO2 it generates is correspondingly -7.5%. Not a separate dispatch/emission-rate error and not closable without re-pinning the gas total to actuals (forbidden, rule #12). Improved vs the nyiso-23 base (whose 2024 gas was -9.0%).

exceptions.metric: C2 gas total vs EIA-930 grid (preliminary-923 vintage)
exceptions.classification: ACCEPTED MEASURED-INPUT LIMITATION (EIA-923 2025 preliminary + basis floor)
exceptions.reason: 2025 EIA-923 is the preliminary M-file (total under-reported; renewables/biomass/oil incomplete, so the scorer carries EIA-930 grid totals for the affected classes). The remaining gas gap is the same EIA-930/EIA-923 basis reconciliation as 2024 plus the preliminary-data incompleteness, not a dispatch error. This run improves 2025 markedly (gas -7.2->-3.9%, within ~1.4pp of the +-2.5% C2 band) by correcting the +2.5 TWh over-import; not chased further with a fitted knob.

exceptions.classification: ACCEPTED MEASURED-INPUT LIMITATION (2024 gas-total basis floor)
exceptions.reason: 2024 is the out-of-scope basis-floor year: the ENTIRE gas total is short by the EIA-923/EIA-930 reconciliation (see the 2024 sysvol exception), so by energy balance the under-run lands on the swing class CC_REGULAR. There is no surplus gas energy for any offer-curve rebalance to allocate (nyiso-22); the class deficit IS the basis floor manifesting, not an offer-curve error. Improved vs nyiso-23 by the import correction; not chased.

exceptions.classification: ACCEPTED MEASURED-INPUT LIMITATION (NYC-peaker reserve-scarcity tail; out of scope)
exceptions.reason: CT_PEAKER under-runs every year because NYC peakers clear on reserve/scarcity (mechanism B / RCPF), not energy — they are priced far above the downstate clearing price (docs/nyiso-dispatch-validation-2026-06.md, nyiso-22). This is the documented scarcity-tail gap, present in every prior NYISO keeper and unrelated to the import boundary flow; an open structural follow-on, not an offer-curve or import-input error.

exceptions.classification: ACCEPTED MEASURED-INPUT LIMITATION (2025 preliminary-923 + basis floor)
exceptions.reason: 2025 gas total is below the preliminary-EIA-923/EIA-930 basis (see the 2025 sysvol exception); the swing class CC_REGULAR carries the residual by energy balance. Improved by the import correction; not an offer-curve error.

exceptions.classification: ACCEPTED MEASURED-INPUT LIMITATION (NYC-peaker reserve-scarcity tail; out of scope)
exceptions.reason: Same NYC-peaker reserve/scarcity-tail gap as the 2024 CT_PEAKER exception; not energy-clearing, unrelated to the import boundary flow.
